context.body: Divine return is pictured through ordinary public life, truth, holiness, and renewed belonging.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The LORD expresses jealous concern for Zion, promises to return, renames Jerusalem by truth and holiness, gathers people, and renews covenant belonging.
observations.label: God returns to dwell in a truthful city: action

observations.body: Old and young fill the streets; scattered people become God’s people.
observations.label: God returns to dwell in a truthful city: response

observations.body: jealous · returned · city of truth · they will be my people
observations.label: Words in Zechariah 8:1–8

payload.posture: Read Zechariah 8:1–8 as future and faithfulness evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The promise speaks to a restored community while its fullest scope remains open in the book’s wider horizon.
payload.title: God returns to dwell in a truthful city
